notes (all non-blocking):
- `packages/integrations/pi/tests/contract.test.ts:399` (built-in finding, accepted as optional): `readRun` and `outcomeOf` are test-local copies of the stream-to-outcome mapping. The real reader of `agent_settled` is outside this repo, in the pi-subagents package. `journal.ts` and `extension.ts` only use the outcome type, `assignmentStatusOf` and `failedFinalMessage`, and the test calls those directly. A change in how a consumer reads the stream cannot fail these tests, but there is no in-repo code to call instead. The `docs/development.md` sentence "feeds each file through the real consumers" overstates this for the json-run cases. It is accurate for `assignmentStatusOf`, `failedFinalMessage` and the extension handlers.
- `contract.test.ts:487` (built-in finding, accepted as optional): the `extension_ui_request` field test asserts on fixture data that `record.ts` wrote. Only the `satisfies RpcExtensionUIRequest` type-check can catch a Pi rename. It cannot fail on consumer behavior, but it does pin the shape the fixtures claim.
- `record.ts:295` (built-in finding, accepted as optional): `satisfies Pick<...>` on `before_agent_start` and `session_compact` leaves fields that Pi later adds or makes required unenforced. This is weaker than the docs' "`mise run check` fails when an update renames or retypes a field". It holds for renames and retypes of the picked fields only.
- `record.ts:439-441` (built-in finding, rejected as a blocker): the walk-up loop has no root guard. It cannot loop in practice, because `Bun.resolveSync` throws first when Pi is not installed and the Pi package root has a `package.json`. A guard would still be tidy.
- `contract.test.ts:143` (built-in finding, optional): the "not edited by hand" test re-renders each file using the version from its own header, so it overlaps the staleness test. The final `expect(installed).toMatch(...)` proves nothing about the files.
- `contract.test.ts:84` (built-in finding, optional): `FixtureHeaderLine` repeats `FixtureHeader` from `record.ts` and is not tied to it. A new header field makes `load` fail loudly, so drift is detected rather than silent.
- Effect-only rule (built-in finding, rejected): `bunfig.toml` applies the async/try/`new Promise` bans only to `packages/runtime/src/**`. Tests are outside that scope and `verify` passes.
- Fixtures are hand-built from Pi's types and rendered by `record.ts`. They are not recorded from a real Pi run, which fits the no-pi-run constraint. `docs/development.md` calls them "recorded", which is loose wording.
- I could only read, not run, the re-record path (`bun packages/integrations/pi/tests/fixtures/record.ts`), because running it writes the fixtures.
- No dist files are in the diff, so there is nothing to compare against a fresh build.
